archetypes.rationale: Regional Bourgogne red: fresh Pinot-led structure intended for earlier assessment than village wines.
Bourgogne village red baseline with moderate tannin, high freshness, and meaningful ageing potential.
Bourgogne Premier Cru red baseline; greater concentration and site expression justify a later, wider window.
Bourgogne Grand Cru red classification baseline with deliberately broad long-ageing bounds.
Regional Bourgogne Chardonnay baseline for earlier assessment and a moderate suggested drink-by year.
Bourgogne Aligote is modeled as light, high-acid, and generally earlier drinking.
Maconnais village white baseline balances ripe Chardonnay body with limestone-supported freshness.
Top Maconnais and Pouilly-Fuisse Premier Cru baseline with more structure and a longer horizon.
Maconnais red baseline is intentionally lighter and earlier than Cote d'Or Pinot Noir.
Cote Chalonnaise village white baseline with fresh Chardonnay structure and medium ageing.
Cote Chalonnaise Premier Cru white baseline extends the village window without equating it to Cote d'Or.
Cote Chalonnaise village red baseline for moderately structured Pinot Noir.
Cote Chalonnaise Premier Cru red baseline with additional concentration and ageing potential.
Cote de Beaune village white baseline with firm acidity and medium-to-long ageing potential.
Bourgogne Premier Cru white baseline calibrated for site concentration, acidity, and a wider window.
Bourgogne Grand Cru white classification baseline with deliberately broad long-ageing bounds.
Beaujolais regional red is modeled for fruit-led early drinking with an early suggested drink-by year.
Aromatic Beaujolais cru baseline for freshness, finesse, and medium ageing.
Structured Beaujolais cru baseline; Morgon and Moulin-a-Vent can improve materially over years.
Languedoc IGP red baseline remains broad and intentionally earlier than named structured appellations.
Structured Languedoc appellation red baseline balancing Mediterranean ripeness and tannin.
Cooler or higher-structure Languedoc cru baseline with a later first assessment and wider horizon.
Dry Languedoc rose baseline intended for early drinking unless a more specific profile says otherwise.
Dry Languedoc white baseline with moderate structure and an intentionally conservative horizon.
Maury red is heterogeneous in the stored data; this low-confidence profile allows for fortified-style longevity without claiming sweetness.
Southern Rhone regional red baseline for ripe Grenache-led blends with moderate ageing.
Southern Rhone cru red baseline with greater concentration, tannin, and long ageing potential.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape red baseline is deliberately broad for structured multi-grape wines with long evolution.
Northern Rhone Syrah baseline combines acidity, tannin, and savory structure for medium-to-long ageing.
Cote-Rotie and Hermitage red baseline requires a later assessment and a deliberately late suggested drink-by year.
Dry Rhone white baseline for rounded texture, moderate acidity, and earlier assessment.
Named Northern Rhone white cru baseline with greater body and medium ageing potential.
Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise sweet-wine baseline; a vintage is still required for calendar advice.
Light dry Alsace white baseline for Pinot Blanc and Sylvaner, emphasizing freshness and earlier drinking.
Aromatic Alsace white baseline for Gewurztraminer and broader Alsace examples.
Alsace Grand Cru Riesling baseline uses high acidity and official long-ageing structure.
Rich Alsace Grand Cru white baseline for Pinot Gris, Gewurztraminer, or unspecified Grand Cru examples.
Dry Centre-Loire Sauvignon baseline emphasizes freshness and a moderate horizon.
Chenin-based Loire white baseline preserves a broad horizon because high acidity can support long evolution.
Sweet Chenin baseline combines high acidity and residual sugar for very long potential.
Loire red baseline is fresh, moderately tannic, and intended for earlier assessment than major long-ageing reds.
Barbera d'Alba baseline uses high acidity, moderate tannin, and medium ageing potential.
Langhe red baseline assumes a structured regional red but remains below Barolo and Barbaresco specificity.
Freisa baseline combines freshness and tannin with medium rather than Barolo-scale ageing.
Moscato d'Asti is modeled as aromatic, sweet, lightly sparkling, and intended for early drinking.
Barolo Nebbiolo baseline retains the owner-accepted long-ageing POC profile.
Barbaresco Nebbiolo baseline retains the owner-accepted POC profile and remains distinct from Barolo.
Chianti red baseline uses Sangiovese freshness and tannin with medium ageing potential.
Chianti Classico baseline reflects higher structure, acidity, and an official ageing hierarchy.
Brunello baseline respects its five-year release age and official 10-to-30-year-plus ageing potential.
Bolgheri red baseline is a curated structured coastal-Tuscan hypothesis pending dedicated consortium evidence.
Broad Toscana IGT red baseline is intentionally low confidence because grape composition is unknown.
Vernaccia di San Gimignano white baseline favors freshness and medium ageing.
Greco di Tufo white baseline is medium-lived and kept separate from the incorrectly stored Toscana area.
Regional Bordeaux red baseline for moderate Cabernet/Merlot structure and medium ageing.
Major left/right-bank Bordeaux appellation baseline with long tannin-supported evolution.
Sauternes sweet-white baseline combines sugar, acidity, and a deliberately very broad horizon.
Dry South-West France white baseline remains conservative where exact sweetness and grape composition are unavailable.
Madiran Tannat baseline uses high tannin and long ageing potential.
Jurancon sec baseline emphasizes high acidity and medium-to-long dry-white evolution.
Bandol Mourvedre baseline requires patience and preserves a wide long-ageing horizon.
Dry Provence rose baseline is intended for early drinking.
Provence white baseline for dry Mediterranean whites with moderate ageing.
Vintage Champagne baseline uses acidity and lees-age structure; non-vintage bottles still require a usable date anchor.
Savoie white baseline emphasizes alpine freshness and earlier assessment.
Mondeuse red baseline combines acidity, peppery tannin, and medium ageing.
Rare Mondeuse blanche is retained as a low-confidence distinct white profile rather than treated as a colour error.
Broad Southern Italy red baseline is deliberately low confidence pending denomination-specific public evidence.
Tokaji stored only as white has unknown sweetness; a broad low-confidence horizon avoids pretending to know the exact style.
Villany red baseline is a low-confidence structured red hypothesis pending a dedicated official source.
